title: The built-in HTTP server sends JS bundles and API JSON uncompressed (vendor bundle 2.09 MB on the wire)
body:
qa#1 · os-bob · session_012dn2AecbS6JEeLdRWSW4AC

Filing gate: ③ a task on the maintainer's word. Asked in session on 2026-11-10, after the full-platform test run listed its improvement suggestions, verbatim: 「立卡处理」.

QA-source: #32135 · browser walk (runner C) · observed beside the clauses
Batch-of: objectstack-ai/objectstack#32135 follow-ups, 15 cards filed on the maintainer's 「立卡处理」

## What we saw

On `os dev` (framework ff04ad81) with `Accept-Encoding: gzip, br`: no `Content-Encoding` on two console JS chunks or on an API JSON response. `vendor-objectstack` is 2.09 MB on the wire, `index` 465 KB, `/meta/object?package=…` 159 KB. A console page loads 106–208 JS files (8–16 MB uncompressed). No compression middleware was found in `plugin-hono-server` or the CLI's serve path. Production-mode `os start` was not measured.

## Proposed change

Serve the console's static assets precompressed (brotli/gzip at build) and compress JSON responses above a size threshold in the Hono server, both on by default; verify on `os start`.

## Business reason

Who: every self-hosted deployment without a CDN or reverse proxy, and remote users on slow links. Cost: the first console load costs several times what it should.

## Reader

Triage first touch; lands in `packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server` and the console build in `packages/console`.

## Duplicate check

`is:issue repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack compression gzip hono` (2 hits, both PM seat posts): no card.
